decisions.reason: As a classic lever-handle line built directly on the firm's strongest architectural-hardware knowledge and manufacturing capabilities, it remains easy to maintain and improve, though its age and lower recent visibility make some portfolio pruning plausible.

This handle design is highly related to the firm's existing knowledge base and can be technically supported with low learning cost, but as a narrower single design in a broad portfolio it faces a meaningful risk of rationalization if demand is not strong enough.

The product still fits the firm's core design and fittings competences and benefits from its in-house R&D and market access, yet as an older standalone design with limited recent prominence it is more exposed than system products to being streamlined out.

The electronic access system matches the firm's strategic move toward digital building organization, and because the firm already has related access-control knowledge and R&D capacity it is well placed to learn from and further develop this flagship platform rather than withdraw it.
